title: The year of sorrow
hook: in one year, he loses both Khadijah and Abu Talib, his wife and his protector
carry: grief is a year, not a day

segments.voice: Yesterday, Najashi, the king who wept at Surah Maryam. Your line was a just king.

Some years take more than one thing from you. The same year the job goes, the parent gets sick. The second loss doesn't just add to the first; it lands on a bruise. For the Prophet ﷺ, some years after the cave, came a year like that. The Muslims had just come through a long boycott, years when Quraysh refused to trade with his whole clan or marry into it, and families went hungry in a narrow valley. It had finally ended. Then, within a short time of each other, the two people who had held him up all his life died.
screen: `SOME YEARS TAKE TWO THINGS.` → `A LONG BOYCOTT, JUST ENDED.` → `THEN, TWO DEATHS.`

segments.voice: First his uncle, Abu Talib, who took him in at eight, raised him, and through years of mounting hostility stood between his nephew and Quraysh, because in that society an attack on him meant answering to his clan. Muslims differ on Abu Talib's faith: Sunni scholars follow a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari that says he died without accepting Islam, while Shi'a Muslims hold that he was a believer. Both remember his protection with honor. Then Khadijah, his wife, who saw him first, who wrapped him in a blanket and said, Allah would never disgrace you. Muslims call it 'am al-huzn, the Year of Sorrow. It didn't end there. With Abu Talib gone, the protection went too, and the insults grew bolder. Ibn Ishaq tells how someone threw dirt on the Prophet's head in the street, and at home one of his daughters washed it off, crying, and he told her: don't cry, my daughter, Allah will protect your father. Nobody is told to hurry past this; the seerah names a whole year after grief. Years later, when the Prophet's baby son Ibrahim died, a hadith in Bukhari says he wept openly and said: the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. There, tears and faith sit side by side. The Qur'an gives words for moments like this, words Muslims say on hearing of a death: “Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.” And another surah: “But lo! with hardship goeth ease.”
screen: `ABU TALIB, HIS PROTECTOR.` · `KHADIJAH, WHO SAW HIM FIRST.` · `'AM AL-HUZN: A YEAR NAMED FOR GRIEF.` · `THE EYES SHED TEARS; THE HEART GRIEVES.` · then, large: `GRIEF IS A YEAR, NOT A DAY.`

segments.voice: If you've had a season when more than one thing went at once, let it come to mind gently, without reliving it: name both things quietly, and let it be as heavy as it is. If you haven't had a year like that, think of someone who is in one now. If you pray, you can say: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we belong to Allah, and to Him we return.
'Am al-huzn, the Year of Sorrow: when he lost both Khadijah and Abu Talib, his wife and his protector.
Your line: grief is a year, not a day. Tomorrow, he looks for help in another town. Day ninety-three.

howItsDone: Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un on hearing of any death or loss; mourning is marked with prayer, visits and food for the bereaved, and tears are understood as mercy, not weakness.

what it means: after years of boycott, he lost his wife and his protector together, and the seerah names a whole year for the grief.
what a scholar hears: Abu Talib's death also ended the clan protection that kept the Prophet safe in Mecca, which is why the insults and the search for help in Ta'if follow.
